transcript.content:
hey, i'm berry.

whenever you're ready, tell me your dream — however it comes back to you.

oh hey! ok so the main thing i remember is being back at my primary school, but the whole place was underwater. like i could breathe fine, and i was just swimming down the corridor instead of walking.

that's such a clear picture, the corridor underwater.

was it quiet down there, or were there school sounds?

it was really quiet, now i think about it. just sort of muffled, like when your ears pop. the water was murky too, blue and green, like looking through a fish tank that needs cleaning. there was light coming down in wobbly beams from above.

wobbly light beams, murky water — feels eerie but not scary, the way you say it.

what did you do next?
i swam to my old classroom. all the desks were covered in seaweed, and the other pupils were little silver fish sitting at the desks. it sounds ridiculous but it felt normal in the dream.

doesn't sound ridiculous at all. the fish at the desks, that would stay with me too.

did they look at you when you came in?

i don't think so? they all just faced the front like normal. at the front was my teacher Mr Hale, in his brown jacket, writing on the board. and then while he was writing, he slowly turned into a huge orange octopus, still holding the chalk in one arm.

the chalk staying in one arm as he changed.

how did that feel, seeing him turn like that?

it was weird but i wasn't scared. more like… oh, right, that's him now. like it had always been heading that way. the bell rang after that, but it came out as a big stream of bubbles going up to the surface.

a bubble bell... that's lovely.

did you leave, or stay?
all the fish swam out of the window at once, so i tried to follow them. that's when i woke up.

so the ending was just being pulled awake right as you went to follow.

what part sticks with you most now?
probably the murky blue-green water with those wobbly light beams. that's the bit that feels the most real when i think back.

that murky water, the beams.

when you picture it now, where does the light touch in the water?

it was coming down from above, like through a skylight or something, but sort of wavy. it didn't light up much, just the corridor a bit, and the beams were all soft and shifting. everything else in the water was darker.

soft and shifting, with the rest in shadow.

you were in the dream as yourself, from what you've said. did you ever see your own body while swimming, or was it more like watching it all happen?
i didn't see myself, it wasn't like watching from outside. i was just there, swimming with my own arms and legs. no idea what i looked like though.

just your own body, seen from the inside — that's how most dreams are.

was anything you held onto or carried with you, something that mattered as you moved through it all?
don't think so. there wasn't anything in my hands. i just remember kicking down the corridor, the water sort of thick.

so you were back at your primary school, all underwater, just swimming down the corridor like it was nothing. it was quiet and muffled, the water murky blue-green with wobbly light beams coming down from above. you swam to your old classroom, desks covered in seaweed, little silver fish sitting at them like pupils. mr hale was at the front in his brown jacket, then he turned into a huge orange octopus still holding the chalk — weird but not scary, just right. the bell came out as bubbles, all the fish swam out the window, and you tried to follow before you woke.

did i get that right, or did i miss anything?

yeah, that's pretty much exactly it. the only thing i'd add is the light was coming down in beams from above, like through water from a fish tank, and the whole place had that murky blue-green colour. but you got it.

good. that's it, then.

is there anything else about the dream you'd want to hold onto?
no, that's the whole thing really. the colour and the light are the parts i'd hold onto.

i've got those.

would you like to see this dream drawn?
yeah, i'd like that.

there are a few ways it could be drawn.

soft watercolour, everything gently swims on the page. faded photograph, like a memory printed too long ago to hold its colour. blue ink wash, the whole dream is held in the density of one blue. or a photograph as your eye saw it, as close to being back there as paper can hold. which feels closest, or would you describe your own?
the blue ink wash feels closest. like the whole dream is one deep blue, with the light coming through it.

i'll start with the underwater primary school, then.

here's how i picture it: the school fully underwater, corridors and rooms open, murky and dim with wobbly light beams coming down from above, everything else in shadow. my guesses: a corridor with light from above, a classroom with its desks, a blackboard, windows.

is anything different, or would you leave the details to me?
that sounds right. the only thing that matters to me is the light beams coming down wobbly from above and the rest in shadow. the rest you can guess.

the wobbly light beams and the shadow — i'll keep those at the heart of it.

i'll get to work.
ok. looking forward to it.

i'm sketching the underwater primary school and mr hale and the chalk now — it'll appear on the right. nothing else is being drawn yet.

as you are — you can tell me a little about yourself — or however i imagine you?
just imagine me however you like, i think that's easier. i don't have much to add.

okay, i'll just picture you as a swimmer in that blue water.

i'm sketching you now — everything will appear on the right over the next minute or two. if anything looks wrong once it's there, just say.
that's the first one done. what do you think, how's it looking?

it's there now, on the right.

does it look the way you remember?
i can't actually see it, but you've described the dream back to me and it matched. if it's the blue wash with wobbly light and shadow, that's how it should look.
it's good to know it matches. i'll keep going with the other parts.
ok.
everyone and everything is sketched now. i'll draw the moments of the dream in order, each carrying on from the ones before it, and they'll appear on the right as they're ready.
hh okay, i'll wait.

okay, no rush.

the first moment's up on the right now, you swimming down the corridor in that thick murky water. does it look the way you saw it?
if it's the corridor with the blue-green thick water and the wobbly light beams coming down, then yeah, that's it.
yeah, that's the first one. the other six are still being drawn, they'll show up on the right as they're ready.
alright, i see. i'll keep checking.

the next moment's up now, you swimming down the corridor towards the classroom.

does it look the way you remember?
yeah, that's fine. as long as it's the same murky water and the light coming down.
good, that's the second one on the right. the other five are still on the way.
okay.

the third moment's up now, you entering the old classroom and seeing it. three of seven are on the right; the other four still to come.

does it look the way you remember?
that should be the part with the desks covered in seaweed and the little silver fish sitting at them. if it's that, then yes.

that's the one, with the seaweed desks and the silver fish. glad it matches.

one moment couldn't be drawn though — all the fish swimming out of the window. there was a problem on our side, and i'm sorry. the other three moments are still being drawn and will show up on the right soon.
aw, that's the one i would've liked to see. it's okay though. anything with the octopus?

nothing with the octopus yet, that comes after this part.

there's a new one up now, Mr Hale in his brown jacket writing on the board. does it look the way you remember?
yeah, if he's at the front in his brown jacket, writing on the board, that's right. though in the dream it didn't last long before he changed.

right, it was just a moment of him writing before the change.

the octopus part is still being drawn, it'll show up on the right soon.
ok. holding the chalk in one arm, that bit matters.

the chalk in one arm, yes. that's the detail that makes it him.

the moment of him slowly turning into the octopus is up now. does it look the way you remember?
i can't see it, but if it shows him mid-change, brown jacket still on him and one arm holding the chalk, that's exactly it.

that's exactly it then, the mid-change with the brown jacket still on and the chalk held in one arm.

the last moment is still being drawn, it'll show up on the right soon.

sound.evidence: it was really quiet, now i think about it. just sort of muffled, like when your ears pop. the water was murky too, blue and green, like looking through a fish tank that needs cleaning. there was light coming down in wobbly beams from above.
